title: WHO describes hearing loss as worse than a 20-decibel threshold in both ears
summary: The World Health Organization describes hearing loss as hearing less well than someone with thresholds of 20 decibels or better in both ears.
body: A World Health Organization fact sheet dated 3 March 2026 describes a person as having hearing loss when they cannot hear as well as someone with normal hearing, which it sets at thresholds of 20 decibels or better in both ears. It says the loss may be mild, moderate, moderately severe, severe, or profound, and may affect one ear or both. This card paraphrases that description only. It is not a hearing test.

sources.title: Deafness and hearing loss
sources.author: World Health Organization
sources.note: WHO fact sheet dated 3 March 2026. Paraphrase only; the page is not CC BY. Supports the description of hearing loss as hearing less well than thresholds of 20 dB or better in both ears, across the mild-to-profound range.
